subject: Biotechnology
title: Codeine and CYP2D6
description: A short lesson to help you apply Codeine and CYP2D6.

hook.text: Codeine is a prodrug — it only works after CYP2D6 converts it to morphine. Some people convert too much.

buildup.text: Poor metabolizers get zero pain relief — ultra-rapid metabolizers produce dangerously high morphine levels.

discovery.text: Infant deaths occurred when breastfeeding mothers who were ultra-rapid metabolizers took codeine — morphine in the milk.

twist.text: The FDA now warns against codeine in children under 12 and nursing mothers — pharmacogenomics drove the policy change.

climax.text: CPIC guidelines recommend alternative analgesics for poor and ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolizers — test before prescribing.

punchline.text: Same drug, wildly different effects — your CYP2D6 genotype decides what codeine does.

quiz.question: Why is codeine dangerous for CYP2D6 ultra-rapid metabolizers?
options: They break down codeine before it can work, getting no pain relief
They convert codeine to morphine too quickly, reaching dangerous blood levels
They are allergic to all opioid medications

details.summary: Codeine requires conversion to morphine by the CYP2D6 enzyme for pain relief. Ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolizers produce dangerous morphine levels from standard doses, while poor metabolizers get no pain relief. This variation has caused fatal overdoses in children and breastfed infants.
details.whyItMatters: CYP2D6 variation makes codeine dangerous for up to 10 percent of the population. Fatal pediatric cases prompted FDA black box warnings. This is pharmacogenomics' clearest example of how genetic testing can prevent adverse drug reactions and deaths.
takeaways: Ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolizers convert codeine to dangerously high morphine levels
Poor metabolizers get zero pain relief from codeine due to no morphine conversion
Fatal pediatric cases led to FDA black box warnings against codeine in children

faq.question: How did codeine cause deaths in children?
faq.answer: Children who were ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolizers converted standard codeine doses into excessive morphine levels. After tonsillectomy, several children died from morphine toxicity. Breastfed infants also died when mothers with ultra-rapid metabolism passed high morphine levels through breast milk.

faq.question: Should codeine be prescribed without genetic testing?
faq.answer: Many guidelines now recommend avoiding codeine in children entirely and using CYP2D6 testing before prescribing in adults. Alternative analgesics that do not depend on CYP2D6 metabolism are safer for ungenotyped patients. Some countries have restricted codeine use in pediatric populations.
